doc.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ron Carter's two-bass band and Piccolo
summary: The first gig at Sweet Basil with a badly out-of-tune piano, and the band's touring.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Then you have a long relationship with Ron Carter. Maybe we can talk about that, because I’m looking at Piccolo, 1977, but the relationship obviously extends beyond that.
Oh yeah. That was – when he put together the band with the two basses, that was the first record. I think that was also the first gig. It was at Sweet Basil. I remember we wore tuxedos.
Broke you in for Sphere. Sphere’s coming up later, with the tuxedos.

Yeah, but I do remember the piano was really bad. It was really out of tune. There was a tuner. He tuned it after each set. That’s how bad it was. As it turned out, the tuner was Akua Dixon, who is a violist.
Oh yeah. I know – no, Akua is a cellist . . .
. . . because his sister Diane plays violin.

Yeah, cello, right. But she tuned the piano every set, the day we were recording, after – whoa, okay. But when you – still, when you listen to it, it was just – but again, it was one of those records that the energy of it – it was a very popular record.
I think I even have the – yeah, I have it.
That band, we were together for a minute. Went to Europe and worked a lot around the country, when it was still possible to do that.
